name: ai-agent-incident-multi-regime
title: AI Agent Incident Across Regimes
description: A seven-stage review of one caller-declared agent incident across three regulatory regimes. Step 1 composes a structured incident record from the declared agent identity, incident description with its severity class, session evidence digests and remediation status (art-379). Step 2 then classifies the autonomy tier and the in-force AI Act obligations the declared deployment carries (art-67). Step 3 then applies the DORA major-incident numeric criteria to the declared impact figures and reports a major or non-major classification with the reporting clock a major finding starts (art-467). Step 4 then scores the declared disruption, affected-user and loss figures against the NIS2 significance criteria and reports a significance verdict (art-144). Step 5 then starts the clock obligations for the regimes the caller declares applicable from one determination timestamp (art-428). Step 6 then builds the post-market monitoring, logging and oversight plan for the declared high-risk deployment as a decision-support draft (art-66). Step 7 then validates the declared agent audit-trail records and returns a conformance result (art-237). Each step computes from its own declared inputs; the order is a review sequence, not a statutory one, and the chain determines no reporting obligation.

steps.handoff: Composes a structured incident record from the declared agent identity, incident description with its severity class, session evidence digests and remediation status, degrading claim strength when identity is missing and flagging a malformed cross-link rather than hiding it; step 2 then classifies the agentic-AI risk the declared deployment carries. Stage 1 of 7.

Classifies the autonomy tier and the in-force AI Act obligations the declared deployment carries, mapping transparency, literacy, oversight and systemic-risk duties; step 3 then applies the DORA major-incident criteria to the declared impact figures. Stage 2 of 7.

Applies the DORA Art. 18 numeric criteria over clients affected, duration, geographical spread, data losses, economic impact, critical services and reputational impact to the declared figures and reports a major or non-major classification with the reporting clock a major finding starts; step 4 then scores the same incident against the NIS2 significance criteria. Stage 3 of 7.

Scores the declared disruption, affected-user and loss figures against the NIS2 significance criteria and reports a significance verdict with the authorities it names; step 5 then starts the clock obligations for the regimes the caller declares applicable. Stage 4 of 7.

Starts the clock obligations for the regimes the caller declares applicable from one hash-anchored determination timestamp, giving each obligation its own attestation slot and stable obligation id; step 6 then builds the post-market monitoring plan for the declared deployment. Stage 5 of 7.

Builds the post-market monitoring, logging, human-oversight and serious-incident reporting path plan for the declared high-risk deployment as a decision-support draft; step 7 then validates the declared audit-trail records. Stage 6 of 7.

Validates the declared agent audit-trail records, checking required fields, chain-link format, signature presence and enum conformance, and returns a conformance result with a completeness score. Final stage.
